data_origin: independent generic mathematical definitions in source; no research data
conventions: All quantities are dimensionless analytic test functions. Grids are x-first with shape (61,35), displayed at the actual 4:2 coordinate aspect. Red/blue represent positive/negative scalar values over [-1,1]; white holes are NaN, not zero. Surface height and color represent different arrays. Stokes components lie on the unit sphere; ellipse color is S3, with no physical propagation convention implied.

data_space_decisions.transformation_status: direct raw analytic samples; interval is illustrative, not statistical uncertainty

data_space_decisions.quantity: signed scalar, vectors, surface height and Stokes texture
data_space_decisions.selected_views: orientation/mask comparison, independent surface channels and polarization

style: explicit documentation geometry; 180 DPI preview; fixed canvas; Arial 8/9 pt

images.title: One specification layer, many views
images.caption: Actual public renderers draw analytic arrays onto caller-owned axes. Each view retains its own data meaning.

images.title: Lines, scatter, ribbons and color
images.caption: The shaded interval is ±0.13 around the analytic signal, used to demonstrate ribbon rendering; it is not measured uncertainty.

images.title: Non-square orientation and a genuine NaN hole
images.caption: A 61 × 35 x-first scalar grid with a circular missing region and a sampled rotational vector field. Colorbar has its own axes, preserving the data rectangle.

images.title: Multi-layer surfaces with separate channels
images.caption: Height is 0.25(x²+0.6y²), with the upper layer shifted by 0.85. Colors encode ±sin(1.6x)cos(2.3y); missing cells remain holes.

images.title: Polarization ellipses and Poincare path
images.caption: The left texture is colored by S3; the right path is colored by progression from t=0 to 2π. All three Stokes components are normalized.
